title: Nagendra Singh v. State of U.P. (theft demand; billing officer and Clause 6.14)
coram: Amreshwar Pratap Sahi and Rajiv Lochan Mehrotra, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; respondent no.3 to examine dues and consider Clause 6.14.
headnote: On a writ challenging harassment despite alleged full payment of bills, where the recovery notice rested on alleged electricity theft, the Court did not quash the demand. It directed the consumer to approach respondent no.3, the officer empowered under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to look into billing grievances. If dues were found cleared, appropriate directions were to issue; if any dues remained, payment could be facilitated under Clause 6.14 in accordance with law.
facts: Nagendra Singh petitioned the Allahabad High Court alleging that he had paid all electricity bills and that nothing remained due, yet the respondents continued to harass him. The recovery notice on record was founded on alleged electricity theft. He relied on a 12 April 2017 judgment in Writ Petition No. 12748 of 2017 to contend that assessment had not been carried out under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 read with the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003, and produced receipts as Annexure 1 to show deposits against billed amounts.

holding_units.holding: Without deciding the theft-based recovery or the claim of full payment, the Court directed the petitioner to approach respondent no.3, the officer empowered under the 2005 Code to look into billing grievances, who shall examine the claim and pass an appropriate order. If dues are found cleared, appropriate directions shall issue; if any dues remain, respondent no.3 may facilitate payment keeping in view Clause 6.14 of the 2005 Code in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner had in fact paid all billed amounts and nothing remained due
not_decided.note: Left to respondent no.3 to examine on the receipts and records.

not_decided.point: Validity of the theft-based recovery notice and of the assessment under the 2005 Code
not_decided.note: The plea that assessment was not in accordance with the Supply Code, 2005 was not decided on merits.

authorities.name: Writ Petition No. 12748 of 2017 (decided 12 April 2017)
authorities.holding: Relied on by the petitioner for the plea that assessment not carried out in accordance with the 2005 Code deserved to be quashed; not applied on the merits.
